weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: masked diffusion models are not new; the core formulation (Algorithms 1-2) applies standard linear masking schedule (t/T) without principled justification for why this diffusion formulation is necessary versus alternative iterative refinement strategies

Symbol-Aware Tokenization (SAT) lacks principled justification: alignment rules (e.g., carets to leftmost symbol) are ad-hoc engineering choices rather than derived from first principles; no exploration of design space or comparison to alternative tokenization schemes

Random-Masking Mutual Learning (RMML) is standard regularization with weak justification: Equation 2 applies straightforward KL divergence without ablating loss component weights or comparing against alternative consistency-promoting approaches; connection between training-time consistency and inference-time stability is asserted but not rigorously established

Baseline comparison concerns: all baselines are reimplemented under authors' pipeline (potentially suboptimal); NAMER results are literature-only without direct comparison on MathWriting; Uni-MuMER (recent VLM baseline) completely absent despite discussion in related work

Inference speed advantage over NAR models is not established: no FPS comparison with NAMER; GryphOne-10 at 73.7 FPS requires multiple iterations while one-shot NAR prediction would likely be faster; T=50 at 21.2 FPS is not real-time

High data requirements significantly limit reproducibility and applicability: requires 630k samples (230k handwritten + 400k synthetic); cannot train on small CROHME alone; synthetic data composition and contribution are unexplored with no ablation on synthetic vs. real data split

Experimental setup and reproducibility gaps: no variance reporting (confidence intervals/std dev) despite averaging over 10 runs; no ablations on masking schedules, loss weights, or hyperparameter sensitivity; fixed 224×224 resolution and maximum sequence length 150 may truncate complex expressions

Limited failure analysis and error categorization: only one qualitative example of ambiguous expressions; no breakdown of improvements by error type (symbolic vs. structural); error recovery experiment (Section 4.9) is somewhat artificial (removing operators)

Training-inference mismatch not thoroughly analyzed: model sees partial corruption during training but full masking at inference; extrapolation behavior to highly corrupted sequences is not carefully studied
Generalization analysis is incomplete: CROHME is held-out but from same domain; no analysis of cross-script or cross-style generalization; no comparison of CROHME vs. MathWriting performance gap

Limited theoretical insight into why iterative diffusion specifically benefits hierarchical mathematical expressions; mechanistic understanding of connection between stochastic remasking and structural consistency is intuitive but not rigorously established

Incomplete inference cost characterization: only FPS reported; missing memory footprint, batch scaling behavior, and wall-clock time; practical implications of length-independent control for typical ≤150 token expressions unclear
